newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rebounds, backwardation slimmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rebounds, backwardation slimmer.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices bounced back by late afternoon trade on Friday after falling sharply over the last two days, traders said.
Firmer naphtha prices were attributed to moderate gains in crude prices overnight, they said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half February was assessed at $229.00/$231.00 after it was sold at $230.00 to a Japanese trading house. In late trading on Thursday, it was indicated at $226.00/228.00.
First-half February was quoted at about $4.00 higher than the second-half February level.

First-half March was offered at $226.00 but there were no firm bids. It was traded once at $223.75 and again at $224.25 on Thursday. The backwardation in naphtha inter-month spreads continued to shrink with first-half February/first-half March discussed at about plus $7.00/8.00.

In middle distillates, a major Japanese refiner was rumoured to have bought 250,000 barrels of dual purpose kerosene cargo to be delivered to Japan's northern major island of Hokkaido in January. The cargo was believed to have been priced at around $2.30 over the mean of Singapore quotes.
